title: Usage normalization proto — sketch for hybrid billing
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal sketch for an alternative billing primitive that normalizes different usage patterns (chat, embeddings, long prompts, repeated short requests) into a single "Normalized Interaction Unit" (NIU) to make bundles and tiers simpler and fairer.

Why we might need this:
- Current token-only pricing favors super-bursty long-token workloads or punish conversational apps that have many short turns.
- Customers building chat UIs + few expensive embedding calls struggle to predict costs across features.
- Want a single headline unit for sales/finance to talk about (like '100k NIUs per month') while keeping behind-the-scenes token and compute sensitivity.

High-level idea (rough):
- NIU = base_unit * (token_factor + context_factor + kv_reuse_discount + model_complexity_multiplier)
- Keep NIU integer-ish so packaging is easier. Sell credits (NIUs) in bundles, allow PAYG conversion to NIU at fixed rates.

Candidate components and how to approximate them (back-of-envelope):
1) token_factor = (in_tokens + out_tokens) / 512  // 512 tokens as baseline unit
2) context_factor = max(1, context_window / 2048)  // penalize very long context that costs more compute
3) kv_reuse_discount = (1 - reuse_fraction)  // if we cache prefixes across repeated calls, reduce cost; reuse_fraction in [0,1]
4) model_complexity_multiplier = 1 for base medium model, 1.6 for large, 0.5 for small/quantized

So NIU approx: NIU = ceil( ( (in+out)/512 ) * context_factor * model_mult * (1 - reuse_frac) )

Simple examples (numbers chosen to be easy):
- Short chat turn: in=40, out=80, context_window=1024, reuse_frac=0.6, model_mult=1
  token_factor = (120)/512 = 0.234 -> ~0.234
  context_factor = 1 (1024 < 2048)
  kv_discount = 0.4 -> NIU ≈ ceil(0.234 * 1 * 1 * 0.4) = ceil(0.0936) = 1 NIU
  -> friendly: frequent short turns round to 1 NIU per turn (easy for UX).

- Long prompt summarization: in=4000, out=600, context_window=4096, reuse_frac=0, model_mult=1.6
  token_factor = 4600/512 = 8.98
  context_factor = 4096/2048 = 2
  kv_discount = 1
  NIU ≈ ceil(8.98 * 2 * 1.6 * 1) = ceil(28.74) = 29 NIUs
  -> maps multi-k token usage to ~30 credit hit, which can feel intuitive.

- Embedding call (single doc 2048 tokens, outputs embedding vector compute-heavy): treat as special path: base_embedding_NIU = ceil( (tokens/512)*2 * model_mult )
  e.g., 2048 tokens, model_mult=1.6 -> (4*2*1.6)=12.8 -> 13 NIUs
  Reason: embeddings consume more compute per token (matrix multiply heavy) so multiplier >1.

Pricing mapping thought (example):
- Price per NIU (list) = $0.0009 (pure example) -> 100k NIUs ~ $90
- Or define tiers: Starter 25k NIU, Pro 250k, Scale 1M with volume discounts and dedicated options.

Why this helps:
- Sales can sell "NIU bundles" that map to expected features (eg 10k conversations/day * 3 NIU/conv => 90k NIU/mo).
- Product can set feature costs in NIU (embedding call = 13 NIU; summarize API = 29 NIU) so customers know budget impact.
- Engineering can convert NIU back to actual runtime costs for accounting.

Questions & open problems (TODOs):
- How to measure/use reuse_fraction in practice? Need server-side telemetry to estimate prefix reuse across requests per-tenant. Edge cases: ephemeral sessions versus persistent memory.
- NIU granularity vs UX: rounding up to 1 NIU for tiny calls is simple, but could overcharge extreme microcalls at scale. Maybe bucket small calls into 1 NIU per X calls.
- How do we present NIU to customers vs tokens? UI: show both (NIU remaining + token-equivalent estimate).
- Model-multipliers: should be table-driven by model family and quantization. Need canonical list.
- Embeddings: separate NIU path or include in same formula? Simpler to special-case embeddings to avoid weird fractional NIUs.

Edge cases to think about:
- Streaming: should we charge NIU on final token output only or incrementally? If streaming, count NIU per shard of output (512-token buckets) to enable real-time debiting.
- Retries/failures: refund logic needed if model fails or customer aborts mid-generation.
- Short-lived sessions with high KV reuse by same prompt template vs long sessions with little reuse — adaptive reuse_fraction per-user might be needed.

Quick cost-reckoner (rough CPU/GPU mapping):
- Map NIU -> average token compute cost. For baseline model: 1 NIU ~= 250 tokens of compute (very rough). Use telemetry to calibrate to $/NIU.
- Use model runtime logs: tokens_generated + FLOP estimates -> unify to dollars and then expose price per NIU.

Next steps (practical):
- Prototype: run 2 weeks of telemetry across hosted API to estimate distribution of NIU under naive formula.
- Compute histogram: NIU per request, per session, per customer. Identify tail behaviors and small-call volumes.
- Play with different baselines (512 vs 256) and context divisor (2048 vs 4096) to smooth rounding.
- Build simple calculator (spreadsheet) for sales to convert expected usage into NIU bundles (input: avg turns/day, avg tokens/turn, pct reuse, embedding calls/day).

Notes-to-self (short):
- Keep formula simple to explain to customers; behind the scenes can be more detailed.
- Consider a 'micro-call credit' for < 64 token requests to avoid nickel-and-diming.
- Discuss with finance on how to show NIU on invoices (line items per feature?).

End of scratch — will loop in Miguel/Eleni when I have the crude telemetry output.
